content: This document does not include all potential drug interactions. It is essential to maintain a comprehensive list of all products you use, including prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, and herbal supplements. Share this list with your healthcare provider and pharmacist to ensure safe and effective treatment. Certain medications can reduce the effectiveness of emergency contraception by lowering the levels of contraceptive hormones in your body, potentially leading to pregnancy. Examples of such drugs include griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin), St. John’s wort, medications for seizures (e.g., barbiturates, carbamazepine, felbamate, phenytoin, primidone, topiramate), and certain HIV medications (e.g., nelfinavir, nevirapine). Overdose with this medication is highly unlikely. However, if someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. For non-emergency situations, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This document is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Side effects such as nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, fatigue, dizziness, changes in vaginal bleeding, breast tenderness, or headache may occur. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. For medical advice about side effects, contact your doctor. Before taking levonorgestrel, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other progestins (e.g., norethindrone), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. It passes into breast milk but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Always consult your healthcare provider for guidance. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Keep a detailed list of all products you use and share it with your healthcare provider and pharmacist. Some drugs may reduce the effectiveness of emergency contraception, increasing the risk of pregnancy. Examples include griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins, St. John’s wort, seizure medications, and certain HIV drugs. For storage, keep the medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, following local guidelines. Do not flush or pour it into drains unless instructed. This information was last revised in May 2024. Always consult your healthcare provider for the most accurate and personalized medical advice.
